claims.claim: Anthropic committed the vp-vnp folder (paper plus Lean 4 formalization) to anthropics/formal-math at 2026-11-23T20:04:44Z and merged PR #51 at 21:43:48Z.
OpenAI's commit 'Add VP != VNP manuscript and Lean.' has author time 2026-11-24T01:14:20Z and changed 3,163 files with 442,736 added lines.
OpenAI's history.md states the VP/VNP result 'was obtained on November 6, 2026'; no artifact-level evidence supports the date.
Anthropic's README says the paper and Lean were written by AI models and no human mathematician has checked the proof, and that no machine checks that Statement.lean says what is claimed.

Anthropic's Statement.lean defines MainTheorem: an absolute c>0 and per-characteristic m0 such that circuits for the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial (every field) and the permanent (char != 2) need more than m^(c (log2 m)^(1/3)) gates.
Anthropic's comparator.json lists five theorems with nanoda enabled and only propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice permitted.
OpenAI's Comparator challenge VPVNP.json targets a single theorem vp_ne_vnp, with nanoda disabled and the three standard axioms permitted.
OpenAI's challenge states vp_ne_vnp as an inequality of the predicates IsVP and IsVNP on families over Fin n x Bool, for any field, with circuits whose binary gates are +, - and *.
OpenAI's paper Theorem 1.1 claims border circuits need exp(Omega((log n)^(5/4))) gates over every field; the Lean formalizes only an exact, qualitative superpolynomial bound.
OpenAI's family-379 Lean scope document lists seven items that remain unformalized, including the explicit grid bound n^Omega((log n)^(1/12)).
Before November 2026 the best lower bound for general arithmetic circuits computing an explicit polynomial was Omega(n log n) (Baur-Strassen).
The permanent is VNP-complete over fields of characteristic other than two; in characteristic two it coincides with the determinant; the Hamiltonian cycle polynomial is VNP-complete over every field.
Lean 4.32.2 (2026-07-28) fixed a kernel bug that could be exploited even when using comparator.
Kevin Buzzard found about 38 of roughly 290 OpenAI papers with Lean code do not state the paper's main theorem in Lean.
The Formal Conjectures project has fixed 291 misformalizations across 7,559 Lean statements.
Lance Fortnow called the result 'for now, the most important computational complexity result of the year' and said it does not imply the Boolean separation.
Scott Aaronson wrote Anthropic's bound is exp(Omega(log^(4/3) n)) and OpenAI's exp(Omega(log^(5/4) n)), both using compression followed by diagonalization.
OpenAI's math repository README describes 730 manuscripts in 375 families as raw research data with about 42% of top-line results formalized.
Anthropic's Lean development is reported at 324 files and 72,932 lines.
Limaye-Srinivasan-Tavenas (2021) proved superpolynomial lower bounds for constant-depth arithmetic circuits, extended to all fields by Forbes (CCC 2024).
